usageNotes: Use this to get the current systemd status of all Proxmox-managed services on a specific node (e.g., pveproxy, pvedaemon, pvestatd, corosync). The node must be online and reachable by the API; calling against an offline node will fail. Requires Sys.Audit on /nodes/{node} — read-only, safe to call at any time for health checks or pre-maintenance validation.

examples.summary: List all service states on node pve1

tips: Check 'active-state' (systemd ActiveState) for high-level health: 'active' is healthy, 'failed' needs attention.
Check 'state' (systemd SubState) for finer detail — 'running' is normal for long-lived services, 'exited' is normal for oneshot units that completed successfully.
Check 'unit-state' (UnitFileState) to distinguish services that are 'disabled' vs 'masked' — masked services cannot be started even manually.
Use this endpoint before performing maintenance (e.g., node shutdown, cluster operations) to confirm all critical services like corosync and pveproxy are running.
The 'service' field is the canonical systemd unit name to pass to service-specific endpoints (start, stop, restart, reload, state).
